title: Sr. Hardware Engineer

Job Summary 
 A Senior Hardware Engineer and future leader who designs embedded product hardware end to end: architecture, power, analog, digital, microcontroller and communication interfaces - and then proves it on the bench. You will take products from requirements to a validated board, working alongside firmware, QA and manufacturing, across medical, industrial and IoT products. The person we are looking for owns the whole board, not just the schematic: they select components with supply and cost in mind, design for the enclosure and the test jig, and treat bring-up as part of design, not someone else s problem. 
 
 Responsibilities 
 
 Architecture and Design 
 Work with the development team and product managers to define product hardware architecture. Design embedded product hardware as per requirements: power supply, analog, digital, microcontroller and communication interface sections. Select components balancing performance, availability, cost and lifecycle. Design and develop schematics in Altium Designer. 
 
 Layout and Manufacturing Hand-off 
 Design PCB layouts in Altium considering EMI/EMC and enclosure requirements, or guide a layout engineer doing so. Generate Gerber files and coordinate with PCB manufacturers on ordering, queries and delivery. Handle component procurement for prototypes and coordinate with the prototype assembly team. 
 
 Bring-up, Debug and Collaboration 
 Lead board bring-up, debugging and problem solving on your designs. Coordinate with the firmware team on hardware-firmware integration and with QA on validation. Mentor junior hardware engineers and review their schematics and layouts. 
 
 Technical Skills Required 
 Hardware Design: 5 to 7 years designing embedded product hardware: discrete, power and microcontroller-based designs. Power Analog: Power supply design (DC-DC, LDO), analog signal conditioning, protection circuits. Altium Designer: Schematic and PCB design; multilayer and mixed-signal boards. Memory Interfaces: Flash, eMMC, SDRAM, DDR2/3/4 design and integration. Interfaces: SPI, I2C, UART on-board; USB, Ethernet external interfaces. Wireless: BLE, Wi-Fi, RF, LoRa integration experience. Bring-up Debug: Board bring-up, systematic fault isolation, bench instruments (oscilloscope, logic analyser, multimeter). Collaboration: Strong communication; comfortable in a fast-paced Agile / Scrum environment. 
 
 Preferred Skills (Added Advantage) 
 Experience on medical devices or other regulated products (CE, FCC, UL, BIS, ISO 13485 awareness). EMI/EMC pre-compliance testing exposure and design-for-compliance practices. Working knowledge of embedded C to aid hardware-firmware debugging. Experience in a product design services or contract development environment. 
 
 Qualifications 
 Engineering graduate in an Electronics-based branch. 5 to 7 years of experience in embedded hardware design. Good verbal and written communication in English. 
 
 What Success Looks Like 
 Your boards go from schematic review to validated bring-up with few surprises. Firmware engineers trust your designs and your judgement during integration debugging. Junior engineers improve measurably from your reviews and mentoring.

 Basic Qualification: BE/B-TECH/MCA/BCA or bachelor's degree in a related subject; formal design qualification (HCI, Interaction Design, Visual Design) strongly preferred 
 Travel Requirements: No 
 Website: www.quloi.com 
 Our mission Our mission is to Quantifying all activities for logistics stakeholders. 
 Our Vision Our vision is to Enable businesses to make the best logistics decisions. 
 Whats the Role? We are looking for a Product Innovation and Design Manager who is equally at home defining a new product concept and opening Figma to prototype it themselves. This is a senior role that combines: the strategic product thinking to identify and incubate new solutions, the hands-on design craft to bring those concepts to life using Figma and AI-powered prototyping tools such as Claude Design, and the management experience to lead and grow Qulois UX team. You will own the full arc from discovery to validated prototype — running user research, shaping product direction, designing and iterating in Figma, and leveraging Claude Design to accelerate high-fidelity prototyping before a single line of production code is written. Once a new module or solution is validated, you need to follow the Product basics and prepare the BRD, PRD and make sure the solution is documented properly. 
 Responsibilities/ Duties 1. Lead New Feature Discovery and Incubation: Identify opportunities for entirely new product modules/features by monitoring industry trends, competitor products, regulatory developments, and evolving logistics standards. Define proof-of-concept criteria and validate new concepts with pilot customers before committing engineering resources to full development. Maintain an innovation backlog — a prioritised pipeline of ideas at different validation stages — reviewed regularly with the Head of Product and leadership. Own the structured Product process from validated new modules to ensuring design assets, and product requirements are fully documented. 2. Design and Prototype Hands-On in Figma and Claude Design: Create wireframes, interaction flows, and high-fidelity UI designs directly in Figma for all new product initiatives and innovation concepts. Use Claude Design to rapidly generate and iterate on prototypes, accelerating the design-to-validation cycle and exploring a broader solution space before committing to a direction. Build and maintain a shared Figma component library and design system that all product surfaces — core and local versions — draw from, ensuring visual and interaction consistency across the platform. Produce handoff-ready design specifications, annotated prototypes, and developer notes that engineering teams can implement without ambiguity. 3. Lead and Develop the UX Team: Manage and mentor the UX team (UX researchers, interaction designers, UI designers), setting clear goals, development plans, and quality standards. Own the UX team roadmap and ensure design capacity is allocated across innovation initiatives, core product enhancements, and local version requirements — coordinated through the AI PM Orchestrator. Conduct structured design reviews and hold a consistently high bar for usability, accessibility, and visual quality across all Quloi product surfaces. Actively develop team members’ skills in AI-assisted design tooling, including Claude Design, as part of the team’s ongoing capability uplift. 4. Drive UX Research for New Solutions: Plan and lead UX research activities (user interviews, usability testing, journey mapping, contextual inquiry) to validate new module concepts at every stage. Synthesise research findings into clear product requirements, design briefs, and prioritised problem statements that both the UX team and engineering can act on. Ensure user insight drives every design decision — from initial concept sketch to final prototype — rather than being a one-time input at the start of discovery. 5. Collaborate Across the PM Organisation: Work with the VP of Product to ensure new modules are architecturally and visually compatible with the existing platform — building on the existing product database rather than rebuilding from scratch. Brief Local Version PMs on new modules entering the pipeline early enough for regional design requirements to be incorporated in the initial Figma files. Participate in cross-PM syncs and AI PM Orchestrator-led workflows covering documentation, Confluence pages, and Jira ticket hygiene. 6. Measure Innovation and Design Impact: Define success metrics at the proof-of-concept stage for each new module (e.g., pilot adoption rate, task completion in usability tests, stakeholder confidence score, prototype-to-build time saved via Claude Design). Track UX team performance including design delivery cycle time, usability test scores, design system adoption rate, and cross-team satisfaction. Report innovation pipeline status, prototype velocity, and UX team throughput to leadership on a regular cadence. 
 Criteria for the Role! Experience: 6+ years of combined Product Management and UX/Design experience. Candidates with only a PM background and no hands-on design craft, or only a design background with no PM experience, will not be considered. Figma Proficiency: Advanced Figma skills are non-negotiable — you must be able to independently produce wireframes, high-fidelity UI designs, interactive prototypes, and a structured component library to a professional standard. Claude Design Experience: Demonstrated experience using Claude Design or equivalent AI-powered prototyping tools to generate, iterate on, and validate product concepts. Ability to brief, prompt, and critically evaluate AI-generated design output. UX Team Management: Minimum 2 years of formal people management responsibility for a UX or product design team, including goal-setting, performance development, and capacity planning. 0-to-1 Product Experience: Proven track record of taking a new product concept from initial idea to validated proof-of-concept in a B2B SaaS environment. Portfolio evidence is required. UX Research Fluency: Hands-on experience planning and conducting user research (not just commissioning it). You know when to run a usability test versus a user interview, and can do both yourself when needed. Design Systems: Experience building and governing a shared component library or design system used by multiple teams or product surfaces. Industry Domain knowledge is a strong advantage: Strong interest in logistics, supply chain, or trade technology; able to understand an industry standard or regulatory document and translate it into a product and design implication. Platform Awareness: Understands multi-tenant SaaS platform architecture at a conceptual level; designs with component reuse, localisation, and scalability in mind from the first wireframe. Communication: Able to present early-stage, ambiguous concepts confidently to senior stakeholders and translate feedback into actionable design and product decisions. Tooling: Figma (advanced), Claude Design, Jira, Confluence. Familiarity with handoff tools (Figma Dev Mode, Zeplin) and user testing platforms (Maze, UserTesting, Lookback) is an advantage.
